language.name: Module language
language.hint: Language of the phone interface for everyone. "Automatic" follows each player's Foundry language. Reloads the page.

volume.name: Phone volume
volume.hint: Volume of the ringtone and message beep on this computer.

ringTimeout.name: Ring duration (seconds)
ringTimeout.hint: After this, the call counts as missed. 0 = rings until answered.

gmFloatingButton.name: Floating button for the GM
gmFloatingButton.hint: A telecom icon showing the number of agents' messages you have not read. Click to open the Network panel; drag to move it.

floatingButton.name: Floating button for players
floatingButton.hint: An always visible phone icon showing the number of unread messages. Click to open the phone; drag to move it.

numberPrefix.name: Phone number prefix
numberPrefix.hint: Start of the numbers given to new devices (555- by default, NC- in Cyberpunk): 555-0123. Numbers ending in 02xx (555-0200 to 555-0299) are never given out: keep them for the NPC directory.

universe.name: Universe
universe.hint: Era or genre of the game: sets the devices offered, their default looks, the phone created for a character who has none (a mobile in Vintage, a smartphone otherwise) and some words. Any setting: everything, as before.

gmLook.name: GM panel theme
gmLook.hint: Look of the GM panel. Auto: follows the universe (Orange haze in Cyberpunk, Classic in Vintage, Ops room otherwise).

welcomeMessage.name: Operator welcome message
welcomeMessage.hint: The first time a player opens a new device, its operator sends a welcome message (a mail on a computer).

team.name: Team: PCs know each other (numbers and emails already shared)
team.hint: PCs' devices show the other PCs' devices in their contacts: numbers on phones, emails on computers.

Directory.Search: Search a name or a number…

Directory.Title: Directory
Directory.Hint: One NPC per line: Name | number, then any of: | public (anyone can look it up), | pin (pinned NPC), | off (unassigned number). Lines starting with # are section titles.
Directory.UnknownHint: This number is linked to nothing: no directory entry, no device.
Directory.Name: Name
Directory.OffHint: Out of service: calls and messages get "not in service", without bothering you.
Directory.PinHint: Pinned NPC: on top of Messages and of the sender list
Directory.PublicHint: Public: anyone can look it up
Directory.NoPrep: Nothing to prepare: any number an agent dials reaches you.
Directory.Purpose: The directory only holds NPCs: fake numbers with no device behind them, answered by you. It is optional: any number an agent dials reaches you anyway. It helps you keep track: name a number (who really answers), make it public (players can look it up), pin it (on top of Messages) or switch it off (out of service). The agents' and places' numbers come from their devices: they are listed in the Directory tab, where you can make them public.

Renamed.Title: Phones & Computers
Renamed.Body: Phone & Terminal is now Phones & Computers. Your devices, histories, contacts and settings have been moved over to the new module.
Renamed.Uninstall: You can now uninstall the old module Phone & Terminal (Add-on Modules screen).
Renamed.Disable: The old module Phone & Terminal is still enabled: disable it in Manage Modules, otherwise phones ring twice. Then uninstall it.

Welcome.Title: Welcome to Phones & Computers
Welcome.PointDevice: To be called or texted, a player's character only needs a device. Give one from the Send tab of the panel, in one click.
Welcome.PointNpc: From the {panel} panel, call or write under any name or number you like. No need to create NPC devices or fill in the directory.
Welcome.PointReply: Players can call or text any number, even a made-up one that is not in the directory: you answer, as whoever you like.
Welcome.NoCharacters: No player has an assigned character. Assign a character to each player (User Configuration), then reopen this window.
Welcome.Reopen: To reopen this window: ? button in the {panel} panel.
Welcome.Sms: Welcome to the {operator} network. Your line is active, your number: {number}.
Welcome.Mail:
Welcome to {operator}
Your mailbox {number} is active. Your messages will arrive here.
Welcome.ReadyBare: {n} agent(s) without a device: give one from the Send tab
Welcome.PointDirectory: The Directory is optional: no number to create, no NPC to set up. It only helps you keep track (name a number, make it public, pin it, switch it off), and fills up as you play.
Welcome.MoreTools: More tools: secure devices, jammer, tracking…

Tour.Title: Phones & Computers: the GM panel
Tour.Description: Call and text players as any NPC.

send.title: Send
send.content: Everything starts here: messages and calls to the players.

recipient.title: Recipient
recipient.content: Pick an agent, then one of their devices; or a place where agents are, and its landline. An agent without a device gets one here in one click.

sender.title: Sender
sender.content: Type the name or number the players will see: an NPC, a made-up number… No NPC device or directory needed. Left empty, the number is hidden.

mode.title: Message or call
mode.content: Send a message, or ring their device. When they answer, play the NPC out loud.

inbox.title: Replies
inbox.content: Players' messages to NPCs land here. You answer as the NPC.

devices.title: Devices
devices.content: Every device: edit, give, lock, or create more (landline, terminal, pager…).

network.title: Network
network.content: Cut the network for the whole table. Messages wait until it is back. The ? button reopens the welcome window.

Features.Title: Advanced features
Features.Hint: Off, they are hidden from the panel and the device windows. Nothing is deleted: switched back on, everything returns.
Features.secureHint: Encrypted calls and messages between secure devices, secure lines with NPCs.
Features.compromisedHint: Mark a device as tapped by the enemy; "what the enemy sees" filter.
Features.jammerHint: A carried device that cuts the network in its scene.
Features.trackingHint: How precisely the network can locate each agent (experimental).

Guide.Title: Getting started
Guide.Open: Ctrl+Shift+P or the floating button opens your device. Press again: your next device.
Guide.Call: Call: type a number or a name, then the phone button. Any number works, even a made-up one.
Guide.Text: Text: open a conversation, or start a new one with any number.
Guide.Contacts: Contacts: the address book in the top bar. In a conversation, add the sender to your contacts.
Guide.Show: Show your screen to the agents in the same scene, or forward a message.
Guide.Next: Nothing ever goes to the chat: everything stays on your devices.
Guide.Credit: Phones & Computers, a Foundry VTT module by Soren
